text:
noah: Hey folks, new joiner here (first week). Trying to follow the k8s onboarding but getting `error: You must be logged in to the server (Unauthorized)` when I run `kubectl get namespaces`. KUBECONFIG is ~/.kube/config. Any quick checks?

infra-bot: Welcome to Redwood! :wave: Quick checklist: 1) run `redwood-cli auth sso` 2) `redwood-cli kubeconfig fetch --env dev` 3) verify `kubectl config current-context` is `redwood-dev`. Docs: https://redwood.internal/onboarding/kubernetes

riley: If current-context is wrong it's usually because minikube or another local context is first. Try `kubectl config get-contexts` and `kubectl config use-context redwood-dev` after fetch. Also ensure your Okta session is active in the browser when running the CLI.

noah: I ran the CLI but it failed silently; looks like the Okta popup didn't open. I'm on a company laptop with popups blocked by the browser policy.

maya: you can use the CLI headless flow: `redwood-cli auth sso --device-code` and paste the code into the Okta URL it gives. Worked for me on locked-down machines.

noah: ok that succeeded. I can see `redwood-dev` in `kubectl config get-contexts` but `kubectl get pods -n infra` returns `forbidden: User "github|noah" cannot list resource "pods" in API group "" in the namespace "infra"`. I think RBAC is needed.

riley: yup, default onboarding gives you read access to `default` and `platform-dev` only. For `infra` you need to request group membership or a temporary role. Open a ticket in #help with your GitHub user and namespaces, or ping infra on this thread and we'll grant a short-lived role.

noah: I'll try ticket. Quick question: what's the naming convention for namespace requests? Do I request `infra` or `infra-dev`?

maya: For dev cluster it's usually `infra` (no suffix). Prod names are `infra-prod`. If you're unsure request both and note purpose.

noah: filed ticket: https://redwood.internal/tickets/INC-2024-356. Tagging infra here so they can expedite.

riley: got it. Granting view role to `github|noah` on `infra` for 12 hours now.

noah: confirmed! `kubectl get pods -n infra` returns list. Thanks everyone. One last ask: any tips on avoiding kubeconfig conflicts? I have multiple projects that generate kubeconfigs.

maya: I keep separate files and merge explicitly: `KUBECONFIG=~/.kube/config:~/.kube/redwood kubeconfig view --flatten > ~/.kube/merged` then `export KUBECONFIG=~/.kube/merged`. And `kubectl config get-contexts` to check. Also avoid tooling that overwrites `~/.kube/config` unless you want that.

noah: perfect. That solved it. Appreciate the speedy onboarding help! :tada:
